:::{#cor-convex-stationary}
#### Stationary points of a convex function are global minimizers

If $f$ is as in @thm-convex-first-order and convex,
then every stationary point $\vx^*$ of $f$ (@def-stationary-point)
is a [global minimizer](algebra.qmd#def-global-minimizer).

:::

::: proof

For every $\vx$,

$$
\ba
f(\vx)
&\ge f(\vx^*) + \tp{\paren{\deriv{\vx} f(\vx^*)}} (\vx - \vx^*)
&& \text{(@eq-supporting-hyperplane with } \vy = \vx^* \text{)}
\\
&= f(\vx^*) + \tp{\vzero} (\vx - \vx^*)
&& \text{(} \vx^* \text{ is stationary)}
\\
&= f(\vx^*).
&& \text{(} \dprod{\vzero}{\vecf{v}} = 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-convex-stationary}
#### A convex function, and a non-convex one

- $f(\vx) = x_1^2 + x_2^2 - 2 x_1$ is convex
  by @thm-convex-hessian, since its Hessian is $2 \matr{I}_2$ (@exm-second-order-condition),
  so its stationary point $\tp{(1, 0)}$ (@exm-stationary-point) is a global minimizer,
  as completing the square showed in @exm-first-order-condition.
- Without convexity, a stationary point need not be a minimizer at all:
  $x_1^2 - x_2^2$ has the stationary point $\vzero$, which is not a minimizer (@exm-first-order-condition).
- The corollary says nothing about whether a minimizer exists:
  $e^{2x_1 + x_2} - x_1$ is convex (@exm-convex-hessian)
  but has no stationary point, and so no local minimizer (@exm-first-order-condition).

:::
